chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ja'far ibn Mu'awiya ibn Wahb from Musa ibn Bakr said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'Our companions say that trimming the mustache and cutting the nails is [specifically] for Friday.' He said, 'Glory be to God, take them whenever you wish on Friday, and if you wish, [do so] on the other days.'

key_terms.أَصْحَابُنَا: Our companions (referring to the jurists/scholars of the time)

ai.seo_question: Is trimming the mustache and cutting nails restricted to Friday in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) corrects a common misconception among the Shia community that specific grooming acts like trimming the mustache and cutting nails are restricted to Friday. He clarifies that these acts are permissible at any time, thereby removing unnecessary temporal restrictions and emphasizing the flexibility of personal hygiene within the broader framework of Friday preparations.
